items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1964-11-28
items.q: that was probably Simeon though, wasn't it?

ctx.x: Yeah, the trio side. Oh, Wolverine.
Wolverine. Yeah, that's it, Wolverine. Turtle Twist is another one, you know, and I'm not all familiar with that too much, but I don't know whether it was, that was probably Simeon though, wasn't it?

items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: these boys like Jimmy Noon and Umar Simeon. It was so much better.

ctx.x: I asked him about Begg Speederbeck. I said, are you familiar with him? He said, yes. I said, have you heard him play? He said, yes, I heard him play. I said, well, was he good? He said, yes, he was good. He wasn't as good as they say he was. That's about his course. He said, no, I've never heard him play. He said, yes, he was good. He said, he wasn't as good as they say.

I was close at the time. I was 38 and was here. I was 20 years old. I was asking him about Frank Teschmaker and all these people. They were all right, but he said, these boys like Jimmy Noon and Umar Simeon. It was so much better. There was no comparison. It's true, of course.

He said, well, he wasn't diplomatic. He knew the true stand for guff, you know. Then there were some, of course, that would needle him. They'd start in, you know. Sorry about it. I think it was Hotlips Page one time. I don't know whether he was needleing him or not, but he meant Hotlips Page. He asked him what he was doing or something like that. And he said, Page replied, says, one of them says, I'm playing Kansas City Jazz now. General Rowe says, Kansas City Jazz.
